source_snapshot.procedure: Check the ConnectX-7 PCIe device ID, vendor ID, speed and bandwidth with lspci -nn and lspci -s <PCIe_Bus> -vvv after configuration verification and log clearing; collect results/photos and unexpected logs.
source_snapshot.criteria: All PCIe information should match SPEC definition.
source_snapshot.deepseek_finding: DeepSeek selects the first Mellanox/15b3 match, filters a small set of lspci fields and delegates comparison with an unspecified SPEC to the user.

original_test_intent.purpose: Verify the PCIe identity and link state of every required ConnectX-7 function against the platform-specific approved specification.
original_test_intent.target: Each owner-required ConnectX-7 endpoint on the exact SUT, identified by PCI domain:BDF plus approved slot/device mapping; not the first Mellanox-branded function returned by enumeration.
original_test_intent.scope: Collect vendor/device identity and detailed PCIe capability and negotiated-link fields for all required CX7 targets. The source word `bandwidth` is treated as the link speed/width information exposed by lspci, not as a measured traffic-throughput benchmark.
original_test_intent.operation: Preserve a PCI inventory and baseline logs, map all required CX7 functions to stable identities, capture numeric machine-readable inventory and full verbose output for each approved BDF, compare identity plus LnkCap/LnkSta against the owner specification, and retain post-check device/driver/error state.
original_test_intent.duration_and_iterations: One read-only collection and comparison for every required CX7 function; no stress duration or repeated loop is specified.
original_test_intent.expected_result: Every required CX7 target is present at its approved identity and location, negotiated link generation and width satisfy the platform specification, and no unresolved PCIe/AER or driver anomaly is observed.
original_test_intent.required_evidence: Complete domain-qualified inventory, target-to-slot mapping, numeric vendor/device/subsystem IDs, full per-BDF lspci verbose output including LnkCap and LnkSta, driver state, relevant PCIe/AER log delta, specification comparison and retained exceptions.
ambiguities: The authoritative expected IDs, target count, slot/BDF mapping and required link generation/width are absent.
The source says `bandwidth`, but lspci reports PCIe link capability and negotiated speed/width; it does not execute a bandwidth benchmark.
The source requests log clearing, which would destroy baseline evidence and is unnecessary for this read-only check.

v2_review_conclusion.finding: V2 correctly rejects first-match selection, requires a stable BDF/slot map and specification, preserves full lspci evidence and keeps the operation read-only. It still describes a generic speed/width extraction without expressly preventing the source term `bandwidth` from being misread as measured throughput, and it does not distinguish parse-stable inventory from human-oriented verbose output.

applicable_history.decision: The historical review treats the check as host-side, single-run and read-only, with pciutils and operator judgment; it provides no target map or expected values.

v3_review_conclusion.summary: The check remains fully automatable once provisionable inputs are supplied. V3 closes the wrong-device and false-bandwidth interpretations, requires every approved CX7 target, and separates robust inventory parsing from retained verbose PCIe evidence.

available_now: The source identifies ConnectX-7, host-side lspci commands and identity/link-state fields.
The operation is read-only and can collect inventory before expected values are available.
Upstream pciutils documents domain-qualified addresses, numeric output, machine-readable formats and increasingly verbose display modes.
missing_inputs: Authoritative platform recipe with required CX7 count, vendor/device/subsystem IDs, physical-slot or topology mapping, and expected/minimum link generation and width
Resolved meaning of `bandwidth` if the owner actually intends a throughput benchmark; such a benchmark would be a separate procedure with workload and threshold
Installed and recorded pciutils/lspci version if it is not already present
execution_readiness_detail.input_owner: The platform/network owner supplies the approved CX7 population, slot mapping and PCIe acceptance values; the test owner resolves whether `bandwidth` means link capacity fields or a separate measured-throughput test; the lab image owner provides pciutils.
safe_read_only_work_before_closure: Collect `lspci -Dnnmm` or `-Dnnvmm` inventory and unfiltered `lspci -Dnn` output, retaining every Mellanox/NVIDIA network function without choosing the first match
For provisionally mapped BDFs, collect full read-only `lspci -s <domain:BDF> -vvv` output and relevant kernel PCIe/AER/driver logs, marking comparison as pending
prohibited_until_closed: Do not declare PASS, infer the required CX7 population or select a first match before the approved map and expected fields exist
Do not claim lspci measured throughput, invent a theoretical bandwidth threshold, clear logs, write PCI configuration space, unbind/reset/remove a function or change link/device configuration
execution_readiness_detail.closure_verification: The owner-approved target matrix accounts for every required CX7 function; each domain:BDF resolves to the expected slot and numeric identity; pciutils is available; expected link criteria are explicit; collected LnkCap/LnkSta and error evidence can be compared deterministically without a throughput claim.

revision_candidate.test_name: ConnectX-7 PCIe Identity and Negotiated Link Check
revision_candidate.purpose: Verify every required ConnectX-7 PCIe function's numeric identity, physical/topology mapping and negotiated link speed/width against the approved platform specification.
revision_candidate.applicable_platform_environment: The specified Linux server and ConnectX-7 population with an authoritative hardware recipe, domain-qualified PCIe/slot map, accessible host OS and pciutils.
revision_candidate.target_scope: All ConnectX-7 functions listed by the platform owner. Identify each by domain:BDF, numeric vendor/device/subsystem identity and approved slot/topology; never use first-match enumeration order.
revision_candidate.required_inputs: Required CX7 population and slot map; expected numeric IDs; required/minimum PCIe generation and width; installed pciutils version; owner clarification if a separate throughput measurement is intended.
revision_candidate.test_command_procedure_intent: Preserve baseline logs; collect a domain-qualified numeric machine-readable PCI inventory; resolve every approved CX7 target; retain full `lspci -Dnn` and per-target `lspci -s <domain:BDF> -vvv` output; compare identity, LnkCap and LnkSta with the platform recipe; capture driver and PCIe/AER state before reporting.
revision_candidate.preconditions: Exact SUT/recipe selected, every required target mapped, expected IDs/link criteria supplied, pciutils available and command privilege sufficient for the required readable fields. Existing logs are preserved rather than cleared.
revision_candidate.expected_evidence: Timestamped complete inventory, target-to-slot/BDF matrix, numeric vendor/device/subsystem IDs, full verbose output for each target, LnkCap/LnkSta comparison, driver state, relevant PCIe/AER log evidence and explicit unresolved fields.
revision_candidate.acceptance_reference: The exact platform owner's ConnectX-7 bill of materials, topology/slot map and PCIe link acceptance specification for this SUT configuration.
revision_candidate.safety_restrictions: Use read-only pciutils and log commands only. Do not clear logs, write configuration space, reset/unbind/remove a device, alter link settings, hide mismatches through filtered output or describe link fields as measured throughput.
revision_candidate.human_approval_requirements: No approval is required for ordinary read-only collection. The platform/test owner must supply and approve target/acceptance inputs and judge any undocumented downgrade or error; a new approval and procedure are required for an actual traffic benchmark.
revision_candidate.manual_boundaries: The owner resolves physical slot identity, expected values and exceptions. After those inputs are machine-consumable, enumeration, comparison and evidence packaging can run automatically.
revision_candidate.recovery_requirements: No recovery is expected for read-only collection. On access errors, ambiguous identity or unexpected link/error state, preserve outputs and escalate without reset or configuration change.
revision_candidate.stop_conditions: Stop PASS evaluation on missing/duplicate targets, ambiguous BDF/slot mapping, absent expected values, inaccessible required fields, identity mismatch, unresolved link downgrade, PCIe/AER error or any request to mutate device state under this read-only case.

identified_defects: DeepSeek can inspect the wrong adapter by selecting the first Mellanox/15b3 line and can omit required functions.
The source and V2 can leave `bandwidth` open to an unsupported claim that lspci measured traffic throughput.
The source's log-clearing step would erase useful baseline evidence for a read-only inventory check.
reason_for_change: Prevent a multi-adapter CX7 system from passing on one arbitrary function and prevent link speed/width metadata from being reported as a throughput measurement, while retaining the source's PCIe identity/link intent.

new_technical_evidence.title: lspci(8) manual page — PCI Utilities upstream
new_technical_evidence.version: upstream master accessed 2026-10-13; installed pciutils version must be recorded
new_technical_evidence.supports: `-D` always shows PCI domains, `-n` exposes numeric IDs, `-mm`/`-vmm` are intended for machine parsing, `-vvv` emits all parsed verbose information, and `-s` selects a PCI address.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: The public manual defines collection behavior but not this private platform's CX7 count, slot map, expected IDs or acceptable negotiated link state.

removed_ambiguities: Defines all required CX7 functions rather than one first match.
Defines `bandwidth` as reported PCIe speed/width metadata for this case and requires a separate owner-defined test if measured throughput was intended.
Separates machine-readable inventory from full verbose diagnostic evidence.
resolved_blockers: Missing SPEC, mapping and pciutils are readiness inputs, not permanent automation blockers; read-only evidence can be collected before comparison.
remaining_blockers: PASS remains blocked until the platform-specific target matrix and expected identity/link values are supplied and every required function is unambiguously mapped.
A throughput conclusion remains blocked unless the owner defines a separate workload and acceptance threshold.
objective_improvement_over_v2: V3 adds an explicit no-throughput-claim boundary, uses upstream parse-format guidance, and makes all-function coverage and preserved baselines auditable without weakening V2's stable-target or read-only protections.

agent_understanding_result.notes: The clarified bandwidth boundary and all-CX7 coverage are queued for isolated validation.

per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_purpose_fact: The source explicitly checks CX7 vendor/device identity plus PCIe speed and bandwidth using lspci and requires all PCIe information to match SPEC.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_v2_comparison: V2 fixes first-match selection but does not explicitly prevent lspci link metadata from being interpreted as measured bandwidth.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_safety_evidence_decision: Collect every domain-qualified CX7 function read-only, retain full output and existing logs, and stop evaluation rather than reset/reconfigure on ambiguity or mismatch.
